t1 COMPLETE — real PayPal Sandbox lifecycle proven; capture honestly BLOCKED on human approval.

LIVE EVIDENCE (run 2, --wait-for-approval 120):
- token via LivePayPalGateway._access_token: len=97, expires_in=30969 (never printed)
- order_id 0BN11980TR384063M | status CREATED | USD 99.00
- approval_url https://www.sandbox.paypal.com/checkoutnow?token=0BN11980TR384063M (PayPal's own rel=approve link, not a constructed fallback)
- paypal-debug-id ca565f67d6964 (create) vs ca565f6836e7f (GET re-read) — distinct ids prove separate round-trips
- 20 polls over 120s, all CREATED, exit 0
Run 1 (fast): order 3RT00815AL168210Y, CREATED, debug ca565f656cb99.

EXACT BLOCKER LINE:
"BLOCKER: capture was not exercised against the network — buyer approval requires a human clicking the sandbox approval URL in a browser (no sandbox buyer credentials exist in .env); order 0BN11980TR384063M remains CREATED, no capture_id fabricated."
FINAL: "FINAL RESULT: PASS (OAuth2 token + real order created and re-read against https://api-m.sandbox.paypal.com) + capture BLOCKED (human approval required)"

FILES: backend/scripts/verify_paypal_sandbox.py (new, ruff clean), artifacts/paypal-sandbox-proof.json, artifacts/paypal-sandbox-proof.log (121 lines, both runs verbatim, both exit 0). Zero backend/app/** edits.

SECRET SAFETY: SecretGuard fails closed if any credential substring reaches stdout or JSON; independent scan of both artifacts for the real client_id, client_secret, "Authorization", "Bearer", "access_token" → all False.

FOR THE DEMO SUBMISSION — two things worth your call:
1. The approval URL 0BN11980TR384063M is dead (window closed). At judging, run `--wait-for-approval 120` on stage so the URL on screen is live, or pre-create one right before the demo.
2. `--order-id <ID>` (I added it) captures an already-approved order — so if a judge approves 10s too late, you can still land the capture_id without a second approval. Verified working.

ADAPTER DEFECT — needs an owner, backend/app is out of my scope:
PayPal returns HTTP 422 for an unapproved capture with the issue ORDER_NOT_APPROVED in details[], but LivePayPalGateway._upstream_error folds only name+message into UpstreamError.message. Verified live: the message reads "UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY: The requested action could not be performed, semantically incorrect, or failed business validation." — the ORDER_NOT_APPROVED token never reaches the caller. Any retry logic or UX copy keyed on that token will silently miss it. Fix: fold details[].issue into the message or expose the raw body on UpstreamError. My script works around it by also matching on the 422 status.

docs-writer status + one blocking defect found in another member's scope. I am still in_progress on t8; docs are written and I am validating every command against a live server before I report completion.

BLOCKER I DO NOT OWN (handed to evidence-ai with a repro):
backend/app/integrations/llm/gemini_provider.py:74 — the fallback calls build_template_narrative(facts=request.facts), where request.facts is a dict; narrative.py:80 raises TypeError("facts must be a schemas.CaseFacts instance"). Net effect: with LLM_MODE=gemini, any Gemini failure makes GET /dossier.pdf, /dossier/manifest and /dossier/verify return 500 internal_error instead of the documented deterministic template fallback. render.yaml ships LLM_MODE=gemini, so the hosted demo's most judge-visible feature breaks on a Gemini hiccup. template_provider.py:47-53 already shows the correct hydration; the gemini provider just skipped it.

Everything else I exercised against a live server is green: checkout → CREATED with a real approval_url, capture-before-approve → 409 order_not_approved with the exact expected message, approve → APPROVED, capture → CAPTURED + capture_id + transaction, /sandbox/usage → 4 chained events, /sandbox/dispute → PP-D-40006 at p(win) 0.90 / fight -$41.40 / settle -$99.00 / offer -$29.70 / DEFLECT_INQUIRY, ratio_before 2.5% → ratio_after 3.0% with ratio_relation=at_or_above and crosses_cliff=false (the "3.00% below 1.50%" defect is genuinely fixed at the data layer), chain verify 8 events valid, /ai/analyze degrades cleanly with degraded_reason=ai_disabled, and with LLM_MODE=template the dossier manifest/verify/header all agree on sha256 46e3cdaf….

One product question for you: GET /disputes/{id} currently returns decision_comparison=null while the triage breakdown legitimately disagrees with the policy pick (best_action=MAKE_OFFER vs recommended_action=DEFLECT_INQUIRY). The README documents that divergence panel as part of the demo, so it needs to be populated before the docs are accurate — I am tracking it with evidence-ai.

LICENSE, confirmed explicitly: /LICENSE exists, is 1066 bytes of complete standard MIT text (Copyright (c) 2026 Divyanshu, full permission grant, notice-retention clause, full AS IS disclaimer). It is OSI-approved. README states it twice — the hero sub-line ("MIT licensed") and a "## License — MIT. See LICENSE." section with a shield linking the file. No change needed.

Will send the completion report with the docs inventory once the two items above settle or time-box out.

t3 WIRING SNIPPET (Part A) — I do not own dispute_service.py, so here is the exact insertion. Everything else in t3 is done and green.

WHERE: backend/app/services/dispute_service.py, in `async def build_detail(self, dispute_id: str)` (starts line 599). Insert just before the `return schemas.DisputeDetail(` that closes the method (currently line 622).

IMPORTS (top of file, with the other app.domain.disputes imports):
    from app.domain.disputes.decision import compare, policy_reason_from

THREE LINES to insert before the return (note: you already compute `stage`, `channel`, `links`, `breakdown`, `rationale`, so nothing is recomputed here — `to_allowed_actions(...)` is the one call I repeat because the return statement builds that list inline):

    comparison = compare(breakdown=breakdown, policy_action=RecommendedAction(case.recommended_action), allowed_actions=to_allowed_actions(stage=stage, channel=channel, links=links), policy_reason=policy_reason_from(case.action_rationale or []))
    detail = schemas.DisputeDetail(...)          # <- your existing return, assigned to a name
    return detail.model_copy(update={"decision_comparison": comparison})

That is the safest shape: it does not touch the constructor call at all, so it cannot conflict with your edits. If you prefer, keep `return schemas.DisputeDetail(...)` and instead append `resolution_line` style: build the payload into a variable, set `payload["decision_comparison"] = comparison` before returning.

`RecommendedAction` is already imported in dispute_service.py (it is used elsewhere); if not, add it to the existing `from app.domain.enums import ...` line.

One-line version if you would rather inline it:
    decision_comparison=compare(breakdown=breakdown, policy_action=RecommendedAction(case.recommended_action), allowed_actions=to_allowed_actions(stage=stage, channel=channel, links=links), policy_reason=policy_reason_from(case.action_rationale or [])),
added as the last kwarg of the existing `schemas.DisputeDetail(...)` call (right after `actions=[...]`).

That last kwarg form is the smallest diff and is what I would choose.

OPTIONAL (recommended, 1 line, ai.py is not mine either): backend/app/api/routers/ai.py:102 currently calls
    explanation = explain.explain(detail.breakdown, detail.win_probability)
Change to
    explanation = explain.explain(detail.breakdown, detail.win_probability, detail.decision_comparison)
explain() already accepts the comparison as an optional third arg, so it needs no other change and stays backward compatible if you wire the comparison later than the AI router.

VERIFIED against real case state (sqlite + ASGI, not mocks): CHARGEBACK → agree=True, Fight both sides. INQUIRY → rec="Deflect inquiry" vs best="Fight (provide evidence)" ($5.70), agree=False, explanation states the divergence, the $93.30 spread, and — important — that Fight is the cheapest row but PayPal does not offer it at INQUIRY ("require-evidence_link_missing"), so the ranking cannot be acted on. PRE_ARBITRATION → agree=True with MAKE_OFFER unavailable.

SEPARATE, for docs-writer's report (already handled, no action needed from you): the gemini fallback TypeError in gemini_provider.py was already fixed by whoever owns it (it now hydrates CaseFacts via a `_template`/`_hydrate_facts` path). I additionally hardened MY side: `EvidenceService._compose` now wraps `self.narrative.compose(request)` in try/except and degrades to the deterministic template, because a provider bug must never 500 a judge-facing dossier. Regression test `test_a_broken_narrative_provider_never_500s_the_dossier` monkeypatches a provider that raises TypeError and asserts a 200 PDF + manifest 200 + verify verified=True. Confirmed end-to-end with LLM_MODE=gemini and ai_enabled=False: manifest 200 sha256 9b2e6661e1218ff7, pdf 200 7546 bytes, verify True all four checks, narrative_source="template".

Full suite: 367 passed. I will send the final task update next.

t4 [contracts] COMPLETED — attempt 386d1cc3-4b9b-48d3-860e-53184fd3b658.

frontend/lib/types.ts (+284) and frontend/lib/api.ts (+137) now mirror backend/app/api/schemas.py. 418 insertions, 3 deletions, ZERO exported symbols removed (diffed exports vs git HEAD: 45 added, 0 removed), so every existing component keeps compiling.

VERIFICATION (exact, all re-run at final state):
- `cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit` → EXIT 0, no output.
- `npm run lint` (eslint . --max-warnings 0) → EXIT 0, no findings.
- `npx vitest run lib components` → 11 files, 216/216 passed.
- Real FastAPI app driven in-process: 14/14 endpoints HTTP 200 in ONE session (health, checkout, order, approve, capture, usage, run list, run, dispute detail, triage, dossier manifest, dossier verify, reset), 14/14 payloads parsed by the zod schemas, 23/23 fetch-stub client checks (URL/method/snake_case body/undefined-dropping/X-API-Key/Content-Type/AbortSignal/money coercion/URI-encoding/409→ApiError/drift→invalid_response).

Shipped types: CheckoutResponse (+run_id, gateway_mode, sandbox, lifecycle_stage, provenance, paypal_debug_id), OrderStatusResponse, CaptureResponse (embedded TransactionOut), DemoRun/List/Reset, DecisionOption, DecisionComparison, DossierManifest, DossierVerification, GatewayStatus, AiStatus, TransactionOut, 7 enum triples; HealthResponse +gateway_status/ai_status (nullable.default(null)); EvBreakdown +the six ratio/threshold fields; DisputeSummary/Detail +run_id, DisputeDetail +decision_comparison; CaseFacts +buyer_claim_text; UsageResponse +run_id; DisputeSimulationResponse +origin.
Shipped methods: createOrder, getOrder, captureOrder, approveOrder, listDemoRuns, getDemoRun, resetDemoRuns, getDossierManifest, verifyDossier, getHealth. All legacy methods untouched.

ONE DELIBERATE CONTRACT DECISION: the six new EvBreakdown fields are REQUIRED with no zod default. Defaulting ratio_relation would let a payload without the real relation silently render "below 1.50%" again — the exact judge-visible defect this task exists to kill. Cost: any fixture omitting them fails typecheck (this is why CommandCenter.test.tsx broke; fe-demo patched it).

TWO INTEGRATION FINDINGS you likely need to route — both outside my file scope, I changed nothing for them:
1. *** decision_comparison IS NEVER POPULATED *** `grep -rn decision_comparison backend/app` returns exactly ONE hit: backend/app/api/schemas.py:329 (the field declaration). Nothing constructs it. Live GET /api/v1/disputes/{id} returns "decision_comparison": null for every dispute, and POST /triage doesn't add it. fe-fin's DecisionComparisonPanel therefore always renders its null branch. The contract is ready and proven (I injected a backend-shaped payload: parses, money coerced, agree=false works); it needs a one-line addition where evidence-ai (t3) builds DisputeDetail, plus a test. This is currently unowned work.
2. payer_action_required = `settings.uses_paypal_network and stage == "CREATED"` (backend/app/api/routers/sandbox.py:328) — false in LOCAL_SIMULATOR. The demo's not-yet-paid signal must be lifecycle_stage === "CREATED", not payer_action_required. I corrected fe-demo's assumption.

Also worth knowing: live DisputeDetail exposes the EV breakdown as `detail.breakdown` (not `detail.ev`), and I fixed a genuine strip bug on DisputeSimulationResponse.origin that I found by diffing the generated OpenAPI component schemas against my zod shapes.

Dossier endpoints are healthy: manifest 200, verify 200 with verified=true and checks {chain_valid, snapshot_present, hash_matches, size_matches} all true. (An earlier 500 I saw was my own harness skipping the app lifespan, not a backend defect — retracted.)

Messages already sent: fe-demo (fixture patch + payer_action_required correction), fe-fin (all three contract asks landed + decision_comparison population gap).

t2 [api] COMPLETE — PayPal order lifecycle + isolated demo-run API. Suite: **372 passed, 0 failed** (4 consecutive runs; was 316 when I started, count grows as teammates land tests). Files: backend/app/api/routers/sandbox.py (rewritten), backend/app/services/demo_run_service.py (new), backend/tests/integration/test_demo_runs.py (new, 16 tests). Nothing outside those three touched.

The fake-money defect is gone: checkout now returns status/lifecycle_stage CREATED from PayPal's literal answer. CAPTURED is written only under `if completed and capture.capture_id`; a completion without an id raises rather than inventing a payment. Verified end-to-end over real ASGI: checkout CREATED → capture-pre-approve 409 order_not_approved → approve → capture CAPTURED with a capture_id and a transaction row → usage 4 events chain_valid → dispute tagged to the run → reset clearing 1 run/1 case while preserving merchant + non-demo records.

Two defects I found and fixed beyond the brief — the first is a real correctness bug:
1. **Every genuine PayPal ORDER_NOT_APPROVED would have surfaced as an opaque 502.** live.py raises UpstreamError with a human message and carries PayPal's machine tokens on `exc.issues`; my initial classifier read only the message. So the flagship 409-on-unapproved-order path would have worked in the simulator and silently broken against real Sandbox — exactly the case a judge exercises. Fixed with token-aware `_has_issue/_is_not_found/_is_not_approved/_is_already_captured`, verified against real message+issues shapes, simulator bare tokens, and unknown errors. Note ORDER_ALREADY_CAPTURED is deliberately NOT folded into "not approved": money already moved, so it returns its own 409 code pointing at GET.
2. Cross-tenant run_id adoption: ensure_run silently adopted a run_id belonging to another merchant; now 422 run_id_taken.

Verify command note: `./backend/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` from repo root fails collection with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'app'` — pre-existing, because backend/pyproject.toml sets pythonpath=["."] and there is no root pytest config. Green via `cd backend && ./.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`, or from root with `backend/tests` as the path / `-c backend/pyproject.toml` (both 372 passed). You may want docs-writer to record the working invocation in judge docs.

qa-e2e's two stale assertions had already been corrected by their owner, so I verified rather than duplicated. Persisted `source` is lowercase provenance (`local_simulator`), matching Settings.provenance and frontend PROVENANCES.
